description.en: This module extends the trajecto ontology with comprehensive spatial analysis capabilities for trajectory proximity detection and spatial relationship modeling.

publisher.value: i-Lab, Department of Cultural Technology and Communication, University of the Aegean

definition.value: A circular or polygonal area around a POI within which trajectory points are considered to be in proximity.

comment.en: A defined spatial zone around a point of interest for proximity detection.
Immediate proximity (typically 0-10 meters).
Manhattan distance metric for grid-based distance calculation.
Algorithm used for spatial proximity analysis.
Low quality spatial analysis with unreliable results.
Interaction based on being within proximity threshold.

definition.value: Contextual information about the spatial environment and relationships relevant to trajectory analysis.

comment.en: Spatial context information for trajectory analysis.
Voronoi diagram-based spatial analysis algorithm.

definition.value: A group of trajectories that exhibit similar spatial proximity patterns to points of interest.

comment.en: A cluster of trajectories based on spatial proximity patterns.
Spatial context in rural environments with low POI density.

definition.value: An analytical process that identifies and measures spatial relationships between trajectory elements and points of interest.

comment.en: A comprehensive analysis of spatial proximity relationships in a trajectory.
K-nearest neighbor algorithm for proximity analysis.
A polygonal proximity zone defined by boundary coordinates.

definition.value: A formalized spatial relationship that describes how trajectory elements relate to entities in space.

comment.en: A spatial relationship between trajectory elements and entities of interest.
Interaction where POI attracts trajectory movement.

Anything with spatial extent, i.e. size, shape, or position.
 e.g. people, places, bowling balls, as well as abstract areas like cubes.
Nearby proximity (typically 50-100 meters).
Classification level for spatial proximity.
Euclidean distance metric for straight-line distance calculation.
Spatial context in urban environments with high POI density.
Spatial context for outdoor trajectory analysis.
High quality spatial analysis with reliable results.
Linear feature showing common trajectory paths.

definition.value: An interaction between trajectory elements and entities based on spatial proximity criteria.

comment.en: Interaction defined by spatial proximity relationships.

definition.value: A structured measurement containing distance values calculated using different metrics.

comment.en: A measurement of distance between spatial entities.
Trajectories that do not fit into any meaningful spatial cluster.
Area with low concentration of trajectory activity.
Area with high concentration of trajectory activity.
Spatial feature extracted from trajectory analysis.
Spatial context for indoor trajectory analysis.
Interaction where POI causes trajectory avoidance.
Medium quality spatial analysis with acceptable results.
A spatial cluster with low density of trajectory points.

definition.value: A structured result containing distance measurements, proximity classifications, and related metadata for a trajectory-POI pair.

comment.en: Result of proximity calculation between a trajectory part and a point of interest.
Close proximity (typically 10-50 meters).
Distant proximity (beyond 200 meters).
Pattern of proximity relationships in trajectory data.
Haversine distance metric accounting for Earth's curvature.

definition.value: A spatial area where a POI demonstrates measurable attraction or influence on movement patterns.

comment.en: A zone where a point of interest has measurable influence on trajectory behavior.
Buffer-based proximity analysis algorithm.
DBSCAN clustering algorithm for spatial analysis.
A point, typically described using a coordinate system relative to Earth, such as WGS84.
Vicinity proximity (typically 100-200 meters).
Interaction where POI influences trajectory behavior.
A circular proximity zone defined by a center point and radius.
A method for calculating distance between spatial points.
Quality assessment of spatial analysis results.
A spatial cluster with high density of trajectory points.
Specifies the point of interest that the proximity result refers to.
Indicates that two trajectories cluster together spatially.
Number of trajectories in the spatial cluster.
Radius of the proximity zone in meters.
Distance value in meters between trajectory part and point of interest.
Measure of spatial cohesion within the cluster (0.0-1.0).
Haversine distance in meters, accounting for Earth's curvature.
Associates a point of interest with its proximity zone definition.
Accuracy measure of the proximity analysis (0.0-1.0).
Manhattan distance in meters.
Normalized proximity score (0.0-1.0) where 1.0 is highest proximity.
Indicates that a proximity zone contains a trajectory part.
Associates a trajectory with its spatial proximity analysis.
Associates a trajectory part with its proximity analysis results.
Associates a trajectory part with its spatial context.
Associates a point of interest with its influence zone.

The relation between something and the point, 
 or other geometrical thing in space, where it is.  For example, the realtionship between
 a radio tower and a Point with a given lat and long.
 Or a relationship between a park and its outline as a closed arc of points, or a road and
 its location as a arc (a sequence of points).
 Clearly in practice there will be limit to the accuracy of any such statement, but one would expect
 an accuracy appropriate for the size of the object and uses such as mapping .
Boolean indicating if the trajectory part is within proximity threshold.
Density measure of the spatial cluster.
Associates a trajectory with a spatial cluster based on proximity patterns.
Specifies the distance metric used in a measurement.
Associates a trajectory part with its spatial relationships.
Euclidean distance in meters.
Indicates spatial interaction between trajectory part and entity.
Timestamp when the proximity analysis was performed.
Rank of proximity (1 = closest) for a trajectory part among all nearby POIs.
Specifies the entity that the spatial relationship involves.
Associates a proximity result with its distance measurement details.
Radius of the influence zone in meters.
